content: Since attention always looks for matching word representations, it operates under the assumption that there is always a match to be found inside the sequences. We provide a theoretical limitation to it and propose another technique called conflict that looks for contrasting relationship between words in two sequences. We empirically verify that our proposed conflict mechanism combined with attention can outperform the performance of attention working solely.
